claude.sample_unit: radiologists (200 mammograms each, three sequential reading conditions)

links.outcome: Automation bias and anchoring bias when AI advice was deliberately wrong (perturbed) in AI-assisted mammography
links.effect: Without explanations, automation bias occurred in 65/180 (36.1%) and anchoring bias in 61/180 (33.9%) of manipulated cases.
links.quote: In the AI-assisted condition without explanations, automation bias occurred in 65/180 (36.1%) and anchoring bias in 61/180 (33.9%) of manipulated cases.

links.outcome: Automation and anchoring bias with vs without saliency-based XAI heatmaps
links.effect: With XAI, automation bias fell to 32/180 (17.8%) and anchoring bias to 31/180 (17.2%); aOR 0.56 (0.44-0.71) and 0.61 (0.48-0.78). Reduced but did not eliminate bias.
links.quote: In mixed-effects models, XAI was associated with lower odds of automation bias (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.44-0.71; p < 0.001) and anchoring-related revision bias (aOR 0.61, 95% CI 0.48-0.78; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Reader diagnostic accuracy unaided versus AI-assisted with XAI, and overreliance on AI
links.effect: On non-manipulated cases, accuracy improved from 724/840 (86.2%) unaided to 757/840 (90.1%) with AI + XAI; bias present when AI was misleading.
links.quote: On the non-manipulated subset, diagnostic accuracy improved from 724/840 (86.2%) in the unaided phase to 757/840 (90.1%) in the AI + XAI phase.

screen.practice: saliency-based explainable AI heatmaps to mitigate automation and anchoring bias
screen.reason: The study tests whether providing saliency-based explainable AI (XAI) heatmaps mitigates automation and anchoring bias among radiologists interpreting mammograms compared to standard AI assistance.
